core_problem_solved: To provide a flexible and configurable logging framework for Java applications, allowing developers to control log message formatting and output destinations (appenders) at runtime.
key_features: Hierarchical loggers based on class names
Support for multiple log levels (DEBUG, INFO, ERROR, etc.)
Configurable appenders for output to console, files, sockets, etc.
Pattern-based layouts for formatting log messages
era_and_niche: The de facto standard logging framework for Java throughout the 2000s, and one of the most widely used and influential Java libraries in history.
reason_for_obsolescence: This library (Log4j 1.x) is **obsolete, unmaintained, and contains known critical security vulnerabilities**. It officially reached its End-Of-Life (EOL) in 2015. The modern, official successor is the complete rewrite, **Log4j 2** (`org.apache.logging.log4j:log4j-core`). The other primary modern alternative is **Logback** (`ch.qos.logback:logback-classic`).
